requirements.title: GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id
requirements.rationale: An operator who sees a replaced outcome needs a read endpoint that shows whether a recoverable backup tip exists.

criteria.condition: an owner, an admin or a PAT holding patches:read or patches:write sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id for an existing patch and refs/hub/replaced/<branch> resolves to a commit in the workspace trunk
criteria.action: return the existing patch object (patchResponse, including any origin_* fields) plus replaced_sha holding the full 40-character commit SHA
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object and a replaced_sha string of 40 hexadecimal characters

setup: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
a stub recovery hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a 40-hex SHA for the patch branch
check.pseudocode: for caller in [owner, admin, pat_read, pat_write]: r = get(path, caller); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA; assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{40}$', r.json.replaced_sha); assert r.json.id == patch.id

criteria.condition: the patch is requested and the backup ref does not exist, or the workspace trunk is not on disk, or no recovery hook is registered
criteria.action: return the patch object without a replaced_sha key
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object; the JSON body contains no replaced_sha key

setup: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
check.pseudocode: for setup in [no_ref_hook, no_trunk_hook, nil_hook]: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json

criteria.condition: the recovery hook returns an error while reading the backup ref
criteria.action: log the failure at warn level and return the patch object without replaced_sha
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object, no replaced_sha key, and one warn-level log entry

setup: a stub hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns an error
a captured log handler
check.pseudocode: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json; assert count(logs, level=WARN) == 1

criteria.condition: the requested patch has status deleted
criteria.action: return the patch object with its deleted status
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with status "deleted"

setup: a patch with status deleted and a non-empty deleted_at
check.pseudocode: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.status == 'deleted'

criteria.condition: the patch id does not exist in the workspace
criteria.action: reject the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error message "patch not found"

setup: an owned workspace with no patch of the requested id
check.pseudocode: r = get('/patches/999999'); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch not found'

criteria.condition: the caller is neither the workspace owner nor an admin
criteria.action: reject the request without revealing the workspace
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error message "workspace not found"

setup: a workspace owned by user A and a patch in it
an authenticated user B who is not an admin
check.pseudocode: r = get(path, as_user_b); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'

criteria.condition: the caller is a PAT that holds neither patches:read nor patches:write
criteria.action: reject the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403

setup: a PAT whose permissions are ["workspaces:read"] only
an owned workspace with a patch
check.pseudocode: r = get(path, pat(['workspaces:read'])); assert r.status == 403

criteria.action: for any other patch endpoint (list, add, update, remove, restore, sync), return a patch object without a replaced_sha key
criteria.contract: no patch object in any response body contains a replaced_sha key

setup: a stub hook that always returns a backup SHA
check.pseudocode: for ep in [list, add, update, restore, sync]: body = call(ep, gen_patch_state()); for p in patch_objects(body): assert 'replaced_sha' not in p

requirements.title: POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin: authorization, preconditions and locking
requirements.rationale: A reset moves a branch, so it must refuse every state in which moving is wrong before it takes the lock or touches git.

criteria.condition: an authorised caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin for an eligible patch and the reset completes
criteria.action: return the patch object as GET renders it (including replaced_sha when a backup exists after the reset) plus rebuild_triggered and, only when a job was enqueued, rebuild_job_id
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the patch object, rebuild_triggered (boolean) and optional rebuild_job_id (string)

setup: a stub hook whose RunReset returns action replaced, SHAs, rebuild_triggered true and job id "job-1" and whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a SHA
an eligible active patch
check.pseudocode: r = post(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.rebuild_triggered == True; assert r.json.rebuild_job_id == 'job-1'; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA

criteria.condition: the caller is a PAT without patches:write, or is neither the owner nor an admin
criteria.action: reject the request before any git operation
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 for a PAT without patches:write; HTTP 404 with message "workspace not found" for a non-owner non-admin

setup: a stub hook counting RunReset calls
check.pseudocode: assert post(path, pat(['patches:read'])).status == 403; r = post(path, other_user); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'; assert hook.calls == 0

criteria.condition: the workspace is not active or is not in carry_patch mode
criteria.action: reject the request with the same 400 messages as handleRestorePatch
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with the "workspace is not active" or "workspace is not in carry_patch mode" message

setup: one archived workspace and one standard-mode workspace, each with a patch id
check.pseudocode: assert post(archived).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not active'; assert post(standard).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not in carry_patch mode'

criteria.condition: the workspace clone_status is not ready
criteria.action: reject the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with message "workspace clone is not ready"

setup: an active carry_patch workspace with clone_status "cloning"
check.pseudocode: r = post(path); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace clone is not ready'; assert hook.calls == 0

criteria.condition: the patch id is unknown, or the patch branch name equals the workspace integration branch
criteria.action: reject the request in that order and never move the integration branch
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with message "patch not found" for an unknown id; HTTP 400 with message "patch branch is the integration branch" for the integration branch

setup: a workspace with integration branch "main"
a patch whose branch_name is "main"
check.pseudocode: assert (post(unknown).status, msg) == (404, 'patch not found'); assert (post(main_patch).status, msg) == (400, 'patch branch is the integration branch'); assert hook.calls == 0

criteria.condition: the patch status is merged_upstream or deleted
criteria.action: reject the request; only active, conflict and disabled patches are eligible
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with message "patch status <status> cannot be reset"

setup: one patch with status merged_upstream and one with status deleted
check.pseudocode: for s in ['merged_upstream','deleted']: r = post(patch_with(s)); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == f'patch status {s} cannot be reset'

criteria.condition: wslock.TryLock(slug) reports the workspace is busy after the preceding checks passed
criteria.action: reject the request without writing any ref; the lock is taken only after the checks succeed and is held for the whole operation
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error type workspace_busy and message "another operation is running on this workspace; retry later"

setup: a real carrypatch recovery hook with a real trunk and a stub fetch recording calls
wslock held for the slug by another operation
check.pseudocode: unlock = wslock.TryLock(slug); r = post(path); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'workspace_busy'; assert fetch.calls == 0; assert refs_before == refs_after

criteria.condition: no recovery hook is registered
criteria.action: reject the reset request
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with message "patch reset is not configured"

setup: the recovery hook is nil
check.pseudocode: RegisterRecoveryHook(nil); r = post(path); assert r.status == 500; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch reset is not configured'

requirements.title: Reset semantics: fetch, compare and move
requirements.rationale: The reset must act on the fork's current tip and discard hub commits only with a backup written first.

criteria.condition: a reset holds the workspace lock
criteria.action: run the single-branch fetch +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch> with origin credentials (GIT_PAT, then GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, then none) in both PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE modes, then resolve the fork tip as refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and the local tip as refs/heads/<branch>^{commit} (possibly absent)
criteria.contract: the fetch is called once per reset with refspec +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>; credentials follow the order GIT_PAT, then username/password, then none; after the fetch the fork tip is read from refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and the local tip from refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}

setup: a real bare fork and real trunk
a stub fetch function recording refspec and credentials
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE set to hub, then origin
credentials in turn: GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, none
check.pseudocode: for mode in ['hub','origin']: for creds in cases: reset(); assert fetch.calls[-1].refspec == '+refs/heads/b:refs/remotes/origin/b'; assert fetch.calls[-1].auth == expected(creds)

criteria.condition: origin credential resolution fails or the single-branch fetch fails for a reason other than a missing branch
criteria.action: write no ref, log the underlying error text and not echo it
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with message "failed to resolve origin credentials" for a credential failure, or message "origin fetch failed" with error type origin_fetch_failed for a fetch failure; every ref is unchanged

setup: a real trunk with a local branch and a backup ref
a log capture
a resolver failing with text "secret-token-xyz", and a fetch stub failing with text "dial tcp 10.0.0.1 refused"
check.pseudocode: r = reset(cred_fail); assert r.status == 502 and r.msg == 'failed to resolve origin credentials'; r = reset(fetch_fail); assert r.json.error.type == 'origin_fetch_failed'; assert 'dial tcp' not in r.body; assert 'dial tcp' in logs; assert snapshot_refs() == before

criteria.condition: the fork does not have the branch
criteria.action: write no ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error type missing_on_origin and message "branch does not exist on origin"; every ref is unchanged

setup: a real bare fork lacking the patch branch
a real trunk holding the branch and a backup ref
the real single-branch fetch classification
check.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'missing_on_origin'; assert r.msg == 'branch does not exist on origin'; assert snapshot_refs() == before

criteria.condition: the local branch is missing, or the local and fork tips are the same commit
criteria.action: when missing, create refs/heads/<branch> at the fork tip with a compare-and-swap create and report action created; when the same commit, write nothing and report action none; write no backup in either case
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with action created or none; refs/hub/replaced/<branch> is unchanged

setup: a real bare fork with the branch
a real trunk once without the local branch and once with it at the fork tip
an existing backup ref in the trunk
check.pseudocode: r = reset(no_local); assert r.action == 'created'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; r = reset(same); assert r.action == 'none'; assert rev(backup) == backup_before

criteria.condition: the local tip is a strict ancestor of the fork tip (GitRunner.IsAncestor on SHAs)
criteria.action: move the local branch to the fork tip, report action fast_forwarded and leave any existing backup ref untouched
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; refs/hub/replaced/<branch> keeps its previous value or stays absent

setup: a real fork whose branch is ahead of the trunk's local branch by two commits
an earlier backup ref pointing at an older discarded commit, and a second case with no backup
check.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.action == 'fast_forwarded'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; assert rev_or_none(backup) == backup_before

criteria.condition: the local tip and fork tip differ and the local tip is not a strict ancestor of the fork tip (diverged, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip)
criteria.action: write the local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, overwriting any earlier backup, then move the local branch to the fork tip and report action replaced
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with action replaced; replaced_sha equals the pre-reset local tip; a repeated replaced reset overwrites the backup

setup: a real fork and trunk with diverged tips
a second scenario where the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip
check.pseudocode: r1 = reset(); assert r1.action == 'replaced' and rev(backup) == local_before; commit_on_local(); r2 = reset(); assert rev(backup) == local_before2 != local_before

criteria.action: for any branch move or creation, use the spec 20 compare-and-swap helper (update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>, never checkout, reset or branch -f) and hard-reset the working tree when the moved branch is the trunk's checked-out branch, so the working tree follows the branch
criteria.contract: the branch write is `update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and no checkout, reset or branch -f command touches the patch branch; when the branch is checked out, HEAD, index and working tree equal the fork tip afterwards, with no dirty state; the branch ref equals the fork tip when the action is not none

setup: a real trunk and bare fork
a git runner wrapper recording every command
check.pseudocode: for g in gen_graphs(): setup(g); reset(); assert not any(c.args[0] in ('checkout','branch') for c in runner.cmds); if checked_out: assert git('status --porcelain') == '' and worktree_matches(fork_tip)

criteria.condition: the compare-and-swap write fails because the ref changed after the SHAs were resolved, or the write fails for any other reason
criteria.action: abort the reset, keep any backup already written, and make no further ref writes
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error type ref_changed and message "patch branch changed during reset; retry" for a lost race; HTTP 500 with message "failed to update patch branch <branch>" for any other failure

setup: a real trunk and fork with diverged tips
a hook point that makes a hub push move the local branch between SHA resolution and the write
a second scenario where update-ref fails for another reason (read-only ref lock)
check.pseudocode: r = reset(with_race); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'ref_changed'; assert rev(backup) == tip_read; r = reset(other_fail); assert r.status == 500 and r.msg == 'failed to update patch branch b'

requirements.title: Reset: persisted sync state and rebuild trigger
requirements.rationale: A branch moved by a reset looks in_sync at the next sync, so the reset must record state and trigger the rebuild itself.

criteria.condition: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is origin
criteria.action: after a reset completes with any action, record the patch via the spec 20 PatchStore method as origin_sync_state in_sync with origin_sha set to the fork tip and origin_synced_at set to the current time
criteria.contract: the patch row has origin_sync_state in_sync; origin_sha equals the fork tip; origin_synced_at is within a few seconds of now

setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
a real PatchStore on a test database
a patch with origin_sync_state diverged
reset scenarios for created, none, fast_forwarded and replaced
check.pseudocode: for action in actions: setup(action); reset(); row = store.get(patch); assert row.origin_sync_state == 'in_sync'; assert row.origin_sha == fork_tip; assert now - row.origin_synced_at < 5s

criteria.condition: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is hub
criteria.action: write no origin sync state
criteria.contract: the origin-state PatchStore method is never called; origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at are unchanged

setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=hub
a patch row with null origin_* columns and a recording PatchStore
check.pseudocode: reset(); assert store.origin_state_calls == 0; assert row_after == row_before

criteria.condition: the reset action is created, fast_forwarded or replaced and the patch status is active or conflict and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not "false"
criteria.action: enqueue a rebuild job with the same type, key slug, group slug:integration_branch, payload builder and deduplication as sync, with SubmittedBy set to the caller
criteria.contract: response rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id set to the new job id

setup: a real job queue
a patch with status active, then one with conflict
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
resets with action created, fast_forwarded and replaced
check.pseudocode: r = reset(); job = queue.get(r.rebuild_job_id); assert job.type == 'rebuild' and job.key == slug and job.group == f'{slug}:{integration}'; assert job.submitted_by == caller; assert r.rebuild_triggered

criteria.condition: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false"
criteria.action: enqueue no rebuild job after a branch move
criteria.contract: response rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id

setup: variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC set to "false"
an active patch whose reset will replace the branch
check.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.rebuild_triggered == False; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 0

criteria.condition: the patch status is disabled
criteria.action: move the branch but enqueue no rebuild job, because the rebuild skips disabled patches
criteria.contract: response rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id

setup: a disabled patch whose branch differs from the fork tip
check.pseudocode: r = reset(disabled_patch); assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert queue.count() == 0; assert not r.rebuild_triggered

criteria.condition: the reset action is none
criteria.action: enqueue no rebuild job
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false

setup: local and fork tips identical
an active patch
check.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and r.action == 'none'; assert not r.rebuild_triggered; assert queue.count() == 0

criteria.condition: the rebuild enqueue is deduplicated by the job queue
criteria.action: leave rebuild_triggered false
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false and no rebuild_job_id

setup: an already queued rebuild job with the same key and group
an active patch whose branch will move
check.pseudocode: enqueue_rebuild(slug); r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 1

criteria.condition: the rebuild enqueue returns an error
criteria.action: log the error and complete the reset
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with rebuild_triggered false; the branch move stays in place

setup: a job queue stub whose Enqueue returns an error
an active patch whose branch will move
check.pseudocode: r = reset(queue=failing); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert logs.contains(ERROR_OR_WARN)

requirements.title: CLI: afc patch reset-to-origin
requirements.rationale: Operators drive recovery from the CLI, so the command must map directly to the endpoint.

criteria.condition: the operator runs afc patch reset-to-origin <workspace-slug> <patch-id>
criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id>/reset-to-origin with no body and print the JSON result
criteria.contract: exit code 0 and the response JSON printed to standard output

setup: a stub HTTP server answering 200 with a patch JSON including replaced_sha
check.pseudocode: out, code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin','ws','7']); assert stub.method == 'POST' and stub.path == '/api/v1/workspaces/ws/patches/7/reset-to-origin'; assert stub.body == ''; assert code == 0; assert json(out) == response

criteria.condition: the number of positional arguments is not exactly two
criteria.action: reject the invocation and send no request
criteria.contract: non-zero exit code and no HTTP request made

setup: a stub HTTP server counting requests
check.pseudocode: for args in [[], ['ws'], ['ws','1','x']]: code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin']+args); assert code != 0; assert stub.requests == 0

criteria.condition: the server answers with an error status
criteria.action: propagate the error through apikit.CLIHandleError with SilenceErrors and SilenceUsage set as for patch restore
criteria.contract: non-zero exit code with the server error message reported

setup: a stub server answering 409 with message "patch status deleted cannot be reset"
a second stub answering 502 origin fetch failed
check.pseudocode: out, err, code = run(...); assert code != 0; assert 'cannot be reset' in err; assert 'Usage:' not in err+out; assert cmd.SilenceErrors and cmd.SilenceUsage

criteria.action: state in the reset-to-origin help text the backup ref refs/hub/replaced/<branch> and the replaced_sha field, and add no flags including no --force
criteria.contract: help contains "refs/hub/replaced/" and "replaced_sha"; the command defines no local flags and no --force flag

setup: the constructed PatchCmd tree
check.pseudocode: c = find(PatchCmd, 'reset-to-origin'); h = help(c); assert 'refs/hub/replaced/' in h and 'replaced_sha' in h; assert c.LocalFlags().lookup('force') is None; assert count(c.LocalNonPersistentFlags()) == 0

requirements.title: Protect refs/hub/replaced/ in the git server
requirements.rationale: Only the hub writes backup refs; a client that could overwrite them would destroy the recovery data.

criteria.condition: a client push creates, updates or deletes a ref whose name starts with refs/hub/replaced/
criteria.action: reject that ref at the spec 22 receive-pack interception point, before the registered pre-receive hook is consulted, and keep the ref's old value
criteria.contract: client sees unpack ok and ng <ref> "refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to"

setup: a running git server over a real trunk with a git:write credential
a pre-receive hook registered that would accept everything
an existing refs/hub/replaced/feature ref
check.pseudocode: out = git_push('+X:refs/hub/replaced/new'); assert 'ng refs/hub/replaced/new refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to' in out; assert hook.calls == 0; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before

criteria.action: for any workspace, any workspace mode, any credential with git:write and any ref name starting with refs/hub/replaced/, reject the push of that ref, whether or not a pre-receive hook is registered
criteria.contract: the ref is rejected with the protected-namespace message; the trunk ref is unchanged

setup: git servers over workspaces in standard and carry_patch modes
with and without a registered pre-receive hook
admin, api key and PAT credentials holding git:write
check.pseudocode: for mode, hook, cred, name, op in product(modes, hooks, creds, gen_names('refs/hub/replaced/'), ops): out = push(op, name); assert rejected(out, name); assert trunk_ref(name) == before

criteria.condition: a single push contains a refs/hub/replaced/ ref and the same push also contains a ref outside the protected namespace
criteria.action: process the other refs as usual and reject only the protected ref
criteria.contract: the normal branch is written and the protected ref keeps its old value

setup: a running git server over a real trunk
an existing backup ref
check.pseudocode: out = push(['X:refs/hub/replaced/feature','X:refs/heads/newbranch']); assert 'ok refs/heads/newbranch' in out and 'ng refs/hub/replaced/feature' in out; assert rev(trunk,'refs/heads/newbranch') == X; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before

criteria.condition: a protected ref is rejected
criteria.action: trigger no head_sha update, no audit entry and no post-push hook for that ref
criteria.contract: head_sha is unchanged; no audit entry is emitted; the post-push hook is not called

setup: a git server wired with a recording head_sha updater, audit emitter and post-push hook
a push containing only a protected ref
check.pseudocode: push('X:refs/hub/replaced/f'); assert head_sha_updates == 0; assert audit.events == []; assert post_push.calls == 0

criteria.action: for any ref name outside refs/hub/replaced/, including other names under refs/hub/, not apply the protected-namespace rule
criteria.contract: the ref is accepted and written; the protected-namespace message never appears

setup: a git server over a real trunk with no pre-receive hook registered
check.pseudocode: for name in gen_names_not_prefixed('refs/hub/replaced/'): out = push('X:'+name); assert 'ok '+name in out; assert 'maintained by the hub' not in out

criteria.condition: a client runs git ls-remote or git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>
criteria.action: advertise the backup ref and serve its commit
criteria.contract: ls-remote lists refs/hub/replaced/<branch> and the fetch succeeds with the backup commit

setup: a running git server over a trunk holding refs/hub/replaced/feature at a commit not reachable from any branch
check.pseudocode: assert (SHA+'\trefs/hub/replaced/feature') in git('ls-remote', url); git('fetch', url, 'refs/hub/replaced/feature'); assert git('rev-parse FETCH_HEAD') == SHA

criteria.action: leave hub-internal writes to refs/hub/replaced/ (sync, reset, removal), which do not pass through a client push, unaffected by the rule
criteria.contract: each internal write succeeds; a client fetch sees the value after each write

setup: a real trunk served by the git server
a hub-internal update-ref and a reset that writes a backup
check.pseudocode: runner.UpdateRef(backup, A); assert fetch(backup) == A; runner.UpdateRef(backup, B); assert fetch(backup) == B; hook.RemoveBackup(slug, b); assert rev_or_none(backup) is None

requirements.title: Backup cleanup on afc patch remove
requirements.rationale: A removed patch must not leave an orphan backup ref behind, and a failed cleanup must not undo a completed delete.

criteria.condition: deletePatchAndCompact succeeds in handleRemovePatch and a recovery hook is registered
criteria.action: ask the hook to delete refs/hub/replaced/<branch> (git update-ref -d), taking the branch name from the patch lookup made before deletion
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 and the backup ref no longer exists

setup: a real trunk holding refs/hub/replaced/<branch>
the real carrypatch recovery hook registered
the patch row for that branch
check.pseudocode: r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert rev_or_none(trunk, backup) is None; assert row_missing(id)

criteria.condition: the backup ref does not exist at removal
criteria.action: treat the removal as a success
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 with no warn log

setup: a real trunk without refs/hub/replaced/<branch>
the real recovery hook
a log capture
check.pseudocode: r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert count(logs, WARN) == 0

criteria.condition: the workspace trunk is not on disk at removal (for example an archived workspace)
criteria.action: treat the removal as a success and log it at info level
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 and one info-level log entry

setup: an archived workspace with no trunk directory on disk
the real recovery hook
a log capture
check.pseudocode: r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert count(logs, INFO, contains='trunk') == 1; assert count(logs, WARN) == 0

criteria.condition: the hook fails to remove the ref for any other reason
criteria.action: log a warn entry with slug, branch and error and not change the response, because the row is already gone
criteria.contract: HTTP 204

setup: a stub hook whose RemoveBackup returns an error
a log capture
check.pseudocode: r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; w = logs.warn(); assert w.slug == slug and w.branch == b and w.error != ''

criteria.condition: the workspace lock is held by a running sync
criteria.action: remove the patch without taking the workspace lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 204, never 409

setup: wslock held for the slug by a simulated sync
a backup ref in the trunk
check.pseudocode: unlock = wslock.TryLock(slug); r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert rev_or_none(backup) is None

criteria.condition: no recovery hook is registered
criteria.action: remove no ref and remove the patch as before
criteria.contract: HTTP 204

setup: the recovery hook is nil
a trunk holding a backup ref
check.pseudocode: RegisterRecoveryHook(nil); r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert rev(backup) == before

criteria.condition: a patch is soft-deleted by a rebuild and later restored with POST .../restore
criteria.action: leave refs/hub/replaced/<branch> untouched by the soft deletion so the restored patch keeps its backup
criteria.contract: the backup ref has the same value before the soft deletion and after the restore

setup: a patch with a backup ref pointing at SHA S
a real SQLPatchStore
